key_insight: Bubble nucleation can be a collective, scale-dependent process: closely spaced sites hydrodynamically shield each other, reducing convective cooling and making activation more stable and reproducible.
engineering_relevance: By tuning cavity spacing to separate near-wall nucleation control from bubble-scale vapor removal, engineers can design boiling surfaces that are more robust and higher performing across changing heat loads.
method: Designed paired-cavity surfaces with intra-pair spacing set to the boundary-layer scale.
Set inter-pair separation to the departure-diameter scale to decouple nucleation from collective vapor removal.
Compared site behavior across spacings to identify excessive, promotive, and isolated departure regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reduced variability and sustained activity at close spacings, supporting a hydrodynamic shielding mechanism that stabilizes nucleation sites.
watch_item: The multiscale spacing strategy may be sensitive to operating conditions and geometry, so performance could shift outside the tested thermal and flow regime.
paper_title: Collective Bubble Nucleation: Scale-Separated Hydrodynamic Control of Site Stability and Vapor Removal
